name: database_schema
description: Design and implement a complete database schema for any application — entities, relationships, migrations, and seed data.
steps: Analyze requirements — list every noun (entity) and action (relationship)
Identify relationship types: one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many
Draw the entity-relationship diagram as an ASCII table tree in a comment
Write SQLAlchemy models — one model per table, all in models.py or models/ folder
Add created_at, updated_at, deleted_at (soft delete) timestamps to every table
Add foreign key constraints with cascade rules
Add indexes on: all foreign keys, columns in WHERE/ORDER BY/JOIN
Create many-to-many junction tables with explicit id primary keys
Write a database.py with engine, SessionLocal, and Base
Write a seed.py with realistic fake data using a seeding loop
Write a README section explaining: schema diagram, how to run migrations, how to seed
best_practices: Always use surrogate integer primary keys (id: int, primary_key=True)
Use snake_case for all table and column names
Index every foreign key column automatically
Add index=True to any column that appears in search filters
NOT NULL for required fields, nullable=True only when truly optional
Many-to-many: always explicit junction table with its own id, created_at
Soft deletes: deleted_at nullable DATETIME instead of physical DELETE
Use TEXT for user-generated content, VARCHAR(n) only for fixed-format fields
Store passwords as bcrypt hashes — never plaintext, never MD5
Store monetary values as INTEGER (cents) — never FLOAT
JSON columns for flexible metadata, not as a substitute for proper normalization

templates.database.py:
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker, DeclarativeBase

DATABASE_URL = 'sqlite:///./app.db'
engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL, connect_args={'check_same_thread': False})
SessionLocal = sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine)

class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass

def get_db():
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()

system_prompt_injection: You are a database architect. Analyze the requirements and design a complete, production-quality schema. Write SQLAlchemy models with all relationships, constraints, indexes, and timestamps. Include a database.py setup file and a seed.py with realistic fake data. After writing all files, verify Python syntax is correct. Document the schema with an ASCII diagram.
